correctness.rationale: Every dominating set on a sunlet contains a member of each core–leaf pair, so sizes n and n+1 have respectively 0 and 1 doubled pairs. Removing selected leaves from an attack cannot increase its surplus. For core attacks, direct neighborhood accounting gives d(U)=2*1_{A in U}+sum of state signs at external reached core indices. The two necessary forbidden run patterns have explicit negative-surplus witnessing attacks. For each permitted pattern, any attack either reaches the doubly selected root (surplus reserve two) or a reached missing C-core can be paired with a reached unselected B or A core (positive sign), giving sufficiency. Distinct anchored word counts are 2n-2 and n-3, yielding n(3n-5). The original-graph checker independently exhausts all selected attacks on every 0- or 1-excess configuration for cycle lengths 3–8 (2292 configuration tests), with reduced charge checks through n=11. This is corroboration; the infinity claim follows from the written proof.

Actual prior-record and literature queries under equivalent names returned no covering result. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not an absolute priority claim.

value.rationale: The natural stability/enumeration problem immediately above the known global security minimum has a nontrivial rigid classification: a single additional selected vertex permits only two monotone-run types or one isolated interior leaf-only vertex. The all-attack quantifier makes the local run obstruction substantive, and the exact n(3n-5) first-excess coefficient quantifies how sharply restricted the space of legal sets remains despite n*2^(n-1) dominating one-excess possibilities. The boundary-charge lemma is a structural technique for secure domination on graphs with private leaves; no new full-polynomial or general-corona theorem is claimed.
